messages:
Alex Park: Hey team — just got an escalated ticket from a customer using batch /v1/rerank. They say returned scores are aligned to the wrong queries (shifted). They sent a request_id: req_0a9f2 and example payload. Original customer report: 'some candidates end up scored for different queries, seems like an offset bug when some queries have zero candidates.'

Sandeep Rao: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the exact payload (sanitized) and the response they got? Also which SDK/version and any proxy in front?

Alex Park: Pasted below (removed PII). They were using node-sdk v0.9.2 and no proxy, direct API.

Alex Park: ```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"query_id": "q1", "text": "find docs about billing", "candidates": ["c1","c2"]},
    {"query_id": "q2", "text": "how to set up webhooks", "candidates": []},
    {"query_id": "q3", "text": "api auth error details", "candidates": ["c3"]}
  ]
}
```

Alex Park: Response (abridged):

```json
{
  "scores": [0.67, 0.22, 0.93],
  "candidate_refs": ["c1","c2","c3"]
}
```

Alex Park: Customer expected per-query buckets: q1 -> [c1,c2] with scores [0.67,0.22], q2 -> [] , q3 -> [c3] with [0.93]. Instead it looks like the second score (0.22) got matched to q3/c3 and 0.93 to nothing. They also got a small 400 earlier: `candidates length mismatch` while retrying.

Jess Rivera: Weird. Our batch rerank contract allows empty candidate lists per query. The runtime flattens candidates and returns a flat scores array plus offsets. Did they get offsets in the response?

Alex Park: They got no offsets field — just flat arrays. That's the user-visible regression. They said this started after last week's runtime release.

Maya Chen: @Sandeep can you check the serializer that emits the offsets param? I think we recently changed the wire format to compress empty lists away (to save bytes). Maybe compression removed empty blocks without recording offsets.

Sandeep Rao: Looking now. I can repro locally with their payload using the production container image (runtime: v2026.03.05). Repro steps I used:

Sandeep Rao: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @payload.json
```

Sandeep Rao: payload.json is exactly the payload Alex pasted. I see logs in /var/log/rerank/requests.log: `req_0a9f2: flattening candidates -> ["c1","c2","c3"] offsets missing, returning scores len=3`. There is a TODO in serializer around `compress_empty_lists=true`.

SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427 (priority: P2) — tag: rerank-batch-offsets. Assigned: EngRuntime Oncall.

EngRuntime Oncall: Jumping in. I suspect the encoder that builds the response metadata is skipping entries when candidates length == 0. The client SDK expects an `offsets` array of length == queries_count + 1. Without it, consumers can't map flat scores back.

Maya Chen: Minimal repro (server-side) shows the bug occurs in this pseudo-code: 

```python
# before: offsets = [0]
for q in queries:
    if len(q.candidates) > 0:
        flat_candidates.extend(q.candidates)
        offsets.append(len(flat_candidates))
    # bug: skip offsets.append when candidates == 0
# client expects offsets len == n_queries + 1
```

Maya Chen: So an empty candidate list yields no offset slot. That's the shift.

Jess Rivera: Nice catch. That also explains the intermittent 400: when client validates candidate counts vs offsets it's strict. Sometimes retries produce 400, sometimes silent shift.

Alex Park: Customer impact: some scoring plumbing broke for ~10% of their batches (those containing empty candidate buckets). They're asking for repro steps to validate patched behavior and an ETA for fix.

Sandeep Rao: I have a local patch where we always append offsets even on zero-length candidates. Unit tests added. Running integration now.

Sandeep Rao: Patch PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/5129 — tests pass locally, integration failing on an unrelated flakey e2e but I can reproduce the fix manually.

Sandeep Rao: Quick mitigation for customers: if they ensure every query has at least one placeholder candidate (e.g., "_empty_placeholder") then mapping stays consistent. Not ideal but workable. I'll message the customer.

EngRuntime Oncall: We need a canary deploy ASAP. @deploy-bot can you promote the canary image runtime:v2026.03.06-canary to us-east-1?

deploy-bot: Deploy request received. Canary deploy started for runtime:v2026.03.06-canary in us-east-1. Track at https://deploys.redwood.internal/12345

EngRuntime Oncall: Canary healthy at 5m. I re-ran the customer's payload against canary and got: ```json
{
  "scores": [0.67,0.22,0.93],
  "candidate_refs": ["c1","c2","c3"],
  "offsets": [0,2,2,3]
}
```

EngRuntime Oncall: offsets now present: mapping is q1->[0,2), q2->[2,2) empty, q3->[2,3) stable. Patch looks good. Rolling to prod in 30m assuming no regressions.

Alex Park: Thanks — I'll tell the customer. Any ask for support team?

Jess Rivera: Please share the canary URL and the deploy ticket. Also ask customer to confirm if they can try the placeholder workaround if they've hit blocking issues right now.

Alex Park: Sent customer the canary URL, deploy ticket, and placeholder workaround. Also offered a short-term credit for the disruption. They're going to test in ~1 hour.

Maya Chen: Follow-up: adding an e2e that includes empty candidate lists across permutations so we don't regress again. Filing RFC to avoid implicit compression of wire format.

SupportBot: INC-2026-0427 updated: status -> monitoring.

EngRuntime Oncall: Prod rollout started and completed. Prod health: green. I will post the PR and changelog to #eng-runtime after merge.

Alex Park: Customer confirmed patch fixed mapping on their end. Closing ticket in 2h after final validation. Great cross-team response — thanks everyone :clap:
